claims.claim: 7. Sync: HabitScheduleEdit is inserted once and tombstoned once, with no updatedAt. Entry rows, including exception rows, merge as whole records by updatedAt (last writer wins, ties keep local). Two devices editing the same occurrence differently: with habit edits both rows are kept and applied in createdAt then uid order, so the later createdAt wins per field, and a tombstone on any device wins. With Entry exceptions, if both edited the same override row (same uid), the later updatedAt wins the whole row. If each device created its own override row, the rows have different uids and both sync in, and expand() then keeps only one per (originalEntryId, originalOccurrenceDate) through associateBy, where the later row in list order wins and updatedAt is not compared.

missed.fact: EditScope.Day is per habit: the edit's refUid names one habit, and byHabit groups by refUid. It is NOT 'every habit on a day'. Claim 2's gloss is wrong.
Week and From scopes carry an optional weekday subset (days), which is what 'chosen weekdays' means. The codec encodes it as WEEK:<monday>[:<days>] and FROM:<date>[:<days>].

Occurrence-scope edits apply only blockUid, time, minutes, sortOrder, skip and deleted. rule, rulePatch, pause and weekDays in an Occurrence edit are ignored. Day, Week and From edits go through DayHabit.apply, which takes all fields. Extra edits are applied on top of dayHabit(...).apply(changes).
A Week scope's weekDays is honored only under Week scope; under any other scope it is nulled (changes.copy(weekDays = null)), so confirmed days never reach later weeks.

Habit edits are not last-writer-wins per row: all live rows are applied in (createdAt, uid) order, so a later edit overrides earlier ones only for the fields it sets. The skip and deleted booleans are sticky until a later edit sets them false.
'Move to another day' (non-weekly) writes TWO edit rows: an Occurrence skip on the old day plus an Extra on the target. The weekly variant writes a single From edit with a new Weekdays rule.
Extra occurrence identity is `x:<edit uid>`, so later Occurrence edits can address an added occurrence by that key.

The exception-row key is the pair (originalEntryId, originalOccurrenceDate), not a unique column. Nothing prevents two live exception rows for the same occurrence. expand() takes one via associateBy, and the others are consumed only if they match the same key. Because the map stores only one per key, the extra row's id is never added to `consumed`, and it then surfaces as an 'orphan' occurrence.

Entry exception rows travel with originalEntryUid. A row whose base has not merged yet resolves to a null originalEntryId, and the code calls this a known gap rather than a decision. It then shows as a plain entry (an orphan).

The only writers of isExceptionSkip = true are the ICS importer's EXDATE handling. EntryEditor.move writes isExceptionSkip = false overrides. There is no UI path that skips one occurrence of a task or event.
Trash cascades to exception rows by matching deletedAt with the base's trashedAt, so exceptions are soft-deleted with the series.
The merge of habit edits skips an edit whose HABIT refUid is a purged habit. An edit whose habit has not arrived yet is stored and does nothing until it does.

HabitBlock is merged LWW by updatedAt with tombstone, unlike HabitScheduleEdit. A standing override edit on one device therefore replaces the whole overrides string on the other, with no per-weekday merge.

The override row is created via entry.copy(...), so it inherits title, estimate, importance and other fields from the base at the moment of override. It does not follow later title edits to the series.
